transcript:
User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Gotcha, thanks for calling in — that’s exactly what we hear from a lot of folks.  

So when a call comes in and you and your team are out on a job, what usually happens to that call — does it ring out, go to voicemail, or something else?
User: It usually goes to voicemail if we're out on a job.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense, and that’s where a lot of work slips through the cracks.  

Those calls that hit voicemail now — do people usually leave a message, or do you feel like most of them just hang up and call the next company?
User: Most go to voicemail, but I feel about 50% would book if we answered.
Agent: Got it, so you’re basically watching half your jobs disappear just because no one can grab the phone.  

Roughly how many calls a week do you think are hitting voicemail instead of getting picked up live?
User: About 8 missed calls a week end up in voicemail.
Agent: That’s really helpful to know — so that’s like 4 solid jobs a week just slipping away if half would’ve booked.  

Are you mainly worried about those daytime calls when you’re on jobs, or do you also get a lot of evening / weekend calls that no one can answer live?
User: It's mainly the daytime calls when we're on jobs, but evenings and weekends are also a concern.
Agent: Yeah, I hear you — so it’s busy days plus the off-hours that are leaking work.  

When one of those callers doesn’t get you live — daytime or after-hours — what do you think they usually do next: wait for you, or just move on to another company?
User: They usually move on to another company if they don't reach us live.
Agent: Right, so that’s basically work and revenue walking straight to your competitors whenever you can’t grab the phone.  

Given that, are you looking for something that can actually answer and book those callers for you when you’re tied up on jobs and after-hours, so they don’t slip away?
User: Yes, I'm definitely interested in something that can help book those callers when we're unavailable.
Agent: Makes sense, that lines up exactly with what we help with.  

Has anyone ever actually walked you through what those missed calls are costing you each week in real dollars?
User: No, I haven't had anyone walk me through the costs in real dollars yet.
Agent: Gotcha, thanks for being open about that.  

So ballpark, what’s your average job worth for you — are we talking more like $300, $600, $1,000 per job?
User: Our average job value is about $2,500.
Agent: Mhm, that’s a solid ticket size — with your numbers, those missed calls are leaking about $43,300 a month in work you could be booking.  

So… it’s a 20‑minute walkthrough where we show you exactly how to plug that gap and turn those missed calls into booked jobs — what’s better for you this week, later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works for me.
Agent: Nice, tomorrow’s perfect.  

First thing, what’s your first name?
User: I'm Susan.
Agent: Got it, Susan.  

And your last name?
Agent: And your last name, Susan?
User: My last name is Park.
Agent: Thanks, Susan Park, perfect.  

What’s the name of your company?
Agent: And what’s the name of your company, Susan?
User: The name of my company is Cornerstone Remodeling.
Agent: Perfect, Cornerstone Remodeling, got it.  

So for tomorrow’s demo, I can get you in as soon as Wednesday at 2:00 or 4:15 Eastern — which one works better for you?
User: I'm in Mountain time, so that would be 12:00 or 2:15 for me. I'll take the 2:15 slot.
Agent: Nice, 2:15 your time works.  

So just to confirm, that’s Wednesday the 26th at 2:15 in the afternoon, Mountain time — does that sound right?
User: Yes, book it. Wednesday the 26th at 2:15 PM Mountain time works perfectly.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Susan, you’re all set — we’ve got you booked for Wednesday the 26th at 2:15 PM Mountain time. You’ll get a text in a moment with the confirmation so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if you ever need to.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?

Alright, really glad you called in — Jay’s looking forward to meeting you and walking through how to stop losing those missed-call jobs. Have a great rest of your day. Bye!
